why: Sightread's 60-second demo: ask what a change breaks, answer with the parsed import graph and without it. Every number was measured on Express with Kimi K3.1 Pro on Cerebras; same model both times.
prompt: If I change lib/application.js, what breaks?

answer.lead: 100 files sit downstream of that one file.
bullets: 99 more, three levels deep, all listed by the graph
the same model named 13 of the 100, in 9.75 s

claim.unit: times faster when it reads the graph
claim.footnote: *Kimi K3.1 Pro on Cerebras, Express repo: 1.23 s with the graph, 9.75 s without. Graph lists all 100 files; the model alone named 13.

thread.text: Parsed the repository · 142 files, 160 internal imports
The list is computed from the import statements, not guessed. Handing it to the model is the whole trick: it answers from evidence instead of rebuilding a hundred-file blast radius from memory.
Asked the same question again with no graph in the prompt
